events.text: Roman consuls begin their year in office.
The Roman Senate posthumously deifies Julius Caesar.
Albert II of Habsburg is crowned King of Hungary.
King Francis I of France succeeds to the French throne.
Scotland begins its numbered year on January 1 instead of March 25.
Charles II is crowned King of Scotland.
John V is crowned King of Portugal.
The French Republican Calendar is abolished.
The United States bans the importation of slaves.
Major-General Lachlan Macquarie officially becomes Governor of New South Wales
The Greek Constitution of 1822 is adopted by the First National Assembly at Epidaurus.
The United Kingdom claims sovereignty over the Falkland Islands.
First Polish stamp is issued.
Porfirio Díaz conquers Mexico City, Mexico.
Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom is proclaimed Empress of India.
Ferdinand de Lesseps begins French construction of the Panama Canal.
Eritrea is consolidated into a colony by the Italian government.
Ellis Island opens to begin processing immigrants into the United States.
Spanish rule ends in Cuba.
Nigeria becomes a British protectorate.
The Republic of China is established.
The Belorussian Communist Organisation is founded as a separate party.
Britain's Railways are grouped into the Big Four: LNER, GWR, SR, and LMS.
The Cristero War begins in Mexico.
Alcatraz Island becomes a United States federal prison.
Safety glass in vehicle windscreens becomes mandatory in the United Kingdom.
The Declaration by United Nations is signed by twenty-six nations.
Standard practice uses this day as the origin of the age scale Before Present
Sudan achieves independence from Egypt and the United Kingdom.
European Economic Community established on this day.
Cameroon achieves independence from France and the United Kingdom.
Cigarette advertisements are banned on American television.
Greece is admitted into the European Community.
The ARPANET officially changes to using the Internet Protocol, creating the Internet.
Brunei becomes independent of the United Kingdom.
David Dinkins is sworn in as New York City's first black mayor.
The North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) comes into effect.
The World Trade Organization goes into effect.
Euro currency becomes legal tender in twelve of the European Union's member states.
Sixty-six people die in a nightclub fire in Bangkok, Thailand.
The Alemanni cross the frozen Rhine in large numbers, invading the Roman Empire.
Georgia becomes the fourth state to ratify the United States Constitution.
The British Institution of Civil Engineers is founded.
Reassertion of British sovereignty over the Falkland Islands.
Russo-Japanese War: The Russian garrison surrenders at Port Arthur, China.
World War II: Manila, Philippines is captured by Japanese forces.
World War II: Nuremberg, Germany is severely bombed by Allied forces.
Panamanian president José Antonio Remón Cantera is assassinated.
Vietnam War: The Viet Cong wins its first major victory.
Ronald Reagan sworn in as Governor of California
Sri Lankan Civil War: The Sri Lanka Navy kill 35-100 civilians on the Jaffna Lagoon.
Joseph Jenkins Roberts is sworn in as the first president of Liberia.
American Civil War: Delaware votes not to secede from the United States.
Construction of the Brooklyn Bridge begins.
Battle of Bapaume, a battle in the Franco-Prussian war occurs.
Sino-French War: Beginning of the Battle of Núi Bop
A magnitude 7.7 earthquake destroys the city of Almaty in Russian Turkestan.
Benito Mussolini announces he is taking dictatorial powers over Italy.
The March of Dimes is established by President Franklin D. Roosevelt.
Proceedings of the U.S. Congress are televised for the first time.
A fire damages the top part of the Eiffel Tower.
The Hamilton Watch Company introduces the first electric watch.
The West Indies Federation is formed.
Alaska is admitted as the 49th U.S. state.
Pope John XXIII excommunicates Fidel Castro.
International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights entered into force.
Apple Computer is incorporated.
Manuel Noriega, former leader of Panama, surrenders to American forces.
The Mars Polar Lander is launched.
Final daily Peanuts comic strip.
Julius Caesar fights Titus Labienus in the Battle of Ruspina.
English Civil War: The Rump Parliament votes to put Charles I on trial.
The Netherlands, Great Britain, and France sign the Triple Alliance.
Great Britain enters the Seven Years' War against Spain and Naples.
Samuel Colt sells his first revolver pistol to the United States government.
The New Apostolic Church is established in Hamburg, Germany.
The Fabian Society is founded in London, England, United Kingdom.
Utah is admitted as the 45th U.S. state.
Burma gains its independence from the United Kingdom.
Korean War: Chinese and North Korean forces capture Seoul.
Sputnik 1 falls to Earth from orbit.
Gypsy opened and closed on Broadway after 120 performances and four previews
Luna 1 becomes the first spacecraft to reach the vicinity of the Moon.
Spirit, a NASA Mars rover, lands successfully on Mars at 04:35 UTC.
Duke Ludovico Sforza conquers Milan.
A great fire occurs in Eindhoven, Netherlands.
Battle of Colmar: The French army beats Brandenburg.
The Prague Party Conference takes place.
The German Workers' Party, which would become the Nazi Party, is founded.
Nellie Tayloe Ross of Wyoming becomes the first female governor in the United States.
Construction of the Golden Gate Bridge begins in San Francisco Bay.
The Daily Mail becomes the first transoceanic newspaper.
The Soviet Union recognizes the new pro-Soviet government of Poland.
United States President Harry S. Truman unveils his Fair Deal program.
The play Waiting for Godot by Samuel Beckett is first performed.
Alexander Dubček comes to power; "Prague Spring" begins in Czechoslovakia.
Cnut the Great is crowned King of England.
Harold Godwinson (or Harold II) is crowned King of England.
Philip of Swabia becomes King of the Romans.
Stephen Uroš III is crowned King of Serbia.
Constantine XI is crowned Byzantine Emperor at Mystras.
King Henry VIII of England marries Anne of Cleves.
The Union of Arras is signed.
Joseph, son of Emperor Leopold I, becomes King of the Romans.
The inauguration of the Musikverein in Vienna, Austria.
German geophysicist Alfred Wegener first presents his theory of continental drift.
New Mexico is admitted to the Union as the 47th U.S. state.
Thomas Edison signs his last patent application.
The first general election ever in Vietnam is held.
Congress certifies George W. Bush winner of 2000 elections.
Alfonso IV becomes King of Portugal.
France takes Calais, the last continental possession of England.
Pope Pius V is elected.
Fire destroys Jamestown, Virginia.
The first American commercial bank, the Bank of North America, opens.
HMS Beagle drops anchor off the Chonos Archipelago.
William Kennedy Dickson receives a patent for motion picture film.
Dáil Éireann ratifies the Anglo-Irish Treaty by a 64-57 vote.
World War II: The siege of the Bataan Peninsula begins.
The United States recognizes the new Cuban government of Fidel Castro.
The Jeep Grand Cherokee is introduced at the Detroit Auto Show.
The Senate trial in the impeachment of U.S. President Bill Clinton begins.
Siyaj K'ak' conquers Waka
Alfred the Great leads a West Saxon army to repel an invasion by Danelaw Vikings.
Louis XII of France marries Anne of Brittany.
Second Jacobite rising: Bonnie Prince Charlie occupies Stirling.
Cape Colony becomes a British colony.
The Democratic Party of the United States is organized.
The United States national debt is zero for the only time.
American Civil War: Second Battle of Springfield
African American men are granted the right to vote in Washington, D.C.
The African National Congress is founded.
Crown Prince Nguyễn Phúc Vĩnh Thuỵ ascends the throne, the last monarch of Vietnam.
World War II: Britain introduces food rationing.
In France a referendum supports Charles de Gaulle's policies in Algeria.
President Lyndon B. Johnson declares a "War on Poverty" in the United States.
Soviet space mission Luna 21 is launched.
Password Plus debuts on NBC.
President George W. Bush signs into law the No Child Left Behind Act.
Ahmad Shah Durrani defeats the Marathas in the Battle of Barari Ghat.
Connecticut becomes the fifth state to ratify the Constitution.
Treaty of Jassy between Russian and Ottoman Empire is signed.
Sir Humphry Davy tests his safety lamp for miners at Hebburn Colliery.
The French Academy of Sciences announces the Daguerreotype photography process.
Anson Jones, the last President of the Republic of Texas, commits suicide.
Umberto I becomes King of Italy.
Battle of Bear Valley: The last battle of the American Indian Wars.
Juan de la Cierva makes the first autogyro flight.
World War II: First flight of the Avro Lancaster.
Julius Caesar crosses the Rubicon, signalling the start of civil war.
Pope Fabian succeeds Anterus to become the twentieth pope of Rome.
Robert Guiscard conquers Palermo.
Archbishop William Laud is beheaded at the Tower of London.
Thomas Paine publishes his pamphlet Common Sense.
The Siege of Dunlap's Station begins near Cincinnati during the Northwest Indian War.
Dutch settlers in Cape Town surrender to the British.
American Civil War: Florida secedes from the Union.
John D. Rockefeller incorporates Standard Oil.
World War I: In the Erzurum Offensive, Russia defeats the Ottoman Empire.
The Treaty of Versailles takes effect, officially ending World War I.
Fritz Lang's futuristic film Metropolis is released in Germany.
World War II: The Greek army captures Kleisoura.
Time Warner is formed by the merger of Time Inc. and Warner Communications.
Theodora is crowned empress of the Byzantine Empire.
Vladislaus II, Duke of Bohemia becomes king of Bohemia.
First recorded lottery in England.
Austrian nobility is granted freedom of religion.
A powerful earthquake destroys parts of Sicily and Malta.
Ching-Thang Khomba is crowned King of Manipur.
William Herschel discovers Titania and Oberon, two moons of Uranus.
The Michigan Territory is created.
Alabama secedes from the United States.
The Anglo-Zulu War begins.
Grand Canyon National Monument is created.
The Kingsland munitions factory explosion occurs as a result of sabotage.
First use of insulin to treat diabetes in a human patient.
Amelia Earhart becomes the first person to fly solo from Hawaii to California.
World War II: The Japanese capture Kuala Lumpur.
Italian-American anarchist Carlo Tresca is assassinated in New York City.
The African Convention is founded in Dakar, Senegal.
An avalanche on Huascarán in Peru causes around 4,000 deaths.
East Pakistan renames itself Bangladesh.
The Gateway Bridge, Brisbane, Queensland, Australia is officially opened.
Over 100 people are killed in the Sidi-Hamed massacre in Algeria.
Gustav I of Sweden is crowned king.
The Royal Aeronautical Society is formed in London.
The National Trust is founded in the United Kingdom.
A long-distance radio message is sent from the Eiffel Tower for the first time.
Hattie Caraway becomes the first woman elected to the United States Senate.
World War II: The Red Army begins the Vistula-Oder Offensive.
Biafra capitulates, ending the Nigerian Civil War.
Nineteen European nations agree to forbid human cloning.
The world's largest ocean liner, RMS Queen Mary 2, makes its maiden voyage.
Deep Impact launches from Cape Canaveral on a Delta II rocket.
Government raids kill 143 Boko Haram fighters in Kolofata, Cameroon.
Nika riots in Constantinople.
Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey is sentenced to death.
The design of the Greek flag is adopted by the First National Assembly at Epidaurus.
The Great Fire of New Orleans begins.
The Treaty of Cahuenga ends the Mexican-American War in California.
Establishment of the Colony of Vancouver Island.
The National Geographic Society is founded in Washington, D.C.
The Independent Labour Party of the United Kingdom holds its first meeting.
Émile Zola's J'accuse…! exposes the Dreyfus affair.
The Rhoads Opera House fire in Boyertown, Pennsylvania kills 171 people.
Henry Ford patents a plastic automobile, which is 30% lighter than a regular car.
First Indochina War: The Battle of Vĩnh Yên begins.
Anti-Muslim riots break out in Calcutta, resulting in 100 deaths.
Johnny Cash performs live at Folsom State Prison
Seraphim is elected Archbishop of Athens and All Greece.
An earthquake hits El Salvador, killing more than 800.
Andrew III of Hungary dies, ending the Árpád dynasty in Hungary.
Spain annexes Cuba.
Napoleon III of France escapes an assassination attempt.
An earthquake in Kingston, Jamaica kills more than 1,000 people.
Norway claims Queen Maud Land in Antarctica.
The first prototype of the MiG-17 makes its maiden flight.
NBC's long-running morning news program Today debuts, with host Dave Garroway.
Josip Broz Tito is inaugurated as the first President of Yugoslavia.
Yemen declares an open war against the terrorist group al-Qaeda.
Elizabeth I is crowned Queen of England in Westminster Abbey, London, England.
The British Museum opens.
University of Notre Dame receives its charter from the state of Indiana.
The first newspaper in Afrikaans, Die Afrikaanse Patriot, is published in Paarl.
James Naismith publishes the rules of basketball.
The Pentagon is dedicated in Arlington, Virginia.
World War II: The Soviet counter-offensive at Voronezh begins.
The Soviet Union launches Soyuz 5.
Muammar Gaddafi is proclaimed premier of Libya.
Gerald Ford's would-be assassin, Sara Jane Moore, is sentenced to life in prison.
Wikipedia, a free wiki content encyclopedia, goes online.
Emir Abd-ar-Rahman III established the Caliphate of Córdoba.
The Medici family is appointed official banker of the Papacy.
Ivan the Terrible becomes Czar of Russia.
Philip II becomes King of Spain.
American Revolutionary War: Battle of Cape St. Vincent.
Virginia enacts the Statute for Religious Freedom authored by Thomas Jefferson.
Peninsular War: The British defeat the French at the Battle of La Coruña.
John C. Frémont is appointed Governor of the new California Territory.
Ernest Shackleton's expedition finds the magnetic South Pole.
The League of Nations holds its first council meeting in Paris, France.
Zeta Phi Beta Sorority Incorporated was founded on the campus of Howard University.
Eleftherios Venizelos becomes Prime Minister of Greece for the fourth time.
Benny Goodman and his band performed in concert at Carnegie Hall in New York City
Adolf Hitler moves into his underground bunker, the so-called Führerbunker.
Hello, Dolly! opened on Broadway, beginning a run of 2,844 performances.
The last Iranian Shah flees Iran with his family for good and relocates to Egypt.
Coalition Forces go to war with Iraq, beginning the Gulf War.
Congolese President Laurent-Désiré Kabila is assassinated by one of his own bodyguards.
King Alfonso III of Aragon invades Menorca.
Pope Gregory XI moves the Papacy back to Rome from Avignon.
France recognizes the Huguenots by the Edict of Saint-Germain.
During the French Wars of Religion, Henry IV of France declares war on Spain.
Maltese patriot Dun Mikiel Xerri, along with a number of other patriots, is executed.
The United States takes possession of Wake Island in the Pacific Ocean.
Captain Robert Falcon Scott reaches the South Pole, one month after Roald Amundsen.
The United States pays Denmark $25 million for the Virgin Islands.
Franco-Thai War: French forces inflict a decisive defeat over the Royal Thai Navy.
World War II: The Vistula-Oder Offensive forces German troops out of Warsaw.
The UN Security Council holds its first session.
The Renville Agreement between the Netherlands and Indonesia is ratified.
The Czech Republic applies for membership of the European Union.
General Magnentius deposes Roman Emperor Constans and proclaims himself Emperor.
Nika riots in Constantinople fail.
King Henry VII of England marries Elizabeth of York, daughter of Edward IV.
Spanish conquistador Francisco Pizarro founds Lima, the capital of Peru.
Pope Pius IV reopens the Council of Trent for its third and final session.
Henry Morgan captures Panama.
Frederick I crowns himself King of Prussia in Königsberg.
Wesley College, Melbourne, is established.
An X-ray generating machine is exhibited for the first time by H. L. Smith.
Ignacy Jan Paderewski becomes Prime Minister of the newly independent Poland.
World War I: The Paris Peace Conference opens in Versailles, France.
Warsaw Ghetto Uprising: The first uprising of Jews in the Warsaw Ghetto.
World War II: Liberation of Kraków, Poland by the Red Army.
Lebanese Christian militias kill at least 1,000 in Karantina, Beirut.
Australia's worst rail disaster occurs at Granville, Sydney killing 83.
Martin Luther King, Jr. Day is officially observed for the first time in all 50 states.
Sierra Leone Civil War is declared over.
Clovis II, king of Neustria and Burgundy, is crowned.
Mirandola surrenders to the French.
Thomas Venner is hanged, drawn and quartered in London.
The second group of ships of the First Fleet arrive at Botany Bay.
Britain occupies the Dutch Cape Colony after the Battle of Blaauwberg.
The British East India Company captures Aden.
Giuseppe Verdi's opera Il trovatore receives its premiere performance in Rome.
Anglo-Egyptian Sudan is formed.
Georges Claude patents the neon discharge tube for use in advertising.
The United States Senate votes against joining the League of Nations.
World War II: The Japanese conquest of Burma begins.
Japan and the United States sign the US-Japan Mutual Security Treaty
President Gerald Ford pardons Iva Toguri D'Aquino (a.k.a. "Tokyo Rose").
Nazi war criminal Klaus Barbie is arrested in Bolivia.
Gulf War: Iraq fires a second Scud missile into Israel, causing 15 injuries.
Czech Republic and Slovakia join the United Nations.
The Hong Kong-based file-sharing website Megaupload is shut down by the FBI.
Duke Wladyslaw Lokietek becomes king of Poland.
Christian II is forced to abdicate as King of Denmark and Norway.
Charles I of England goes on trial for treason and other "high crimes".
Hong Kong Island is occupied by the British.
The United States Senate allows the Navy to lease Pearl Harbor as a naval base.
The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) is founded.
Edward VIII becomes King of the United Kingdom.
Sweden and Prussia sign the Treaty of Stockholm.
The Teatro Filarmonico in Verona is destroyed by fire. It is rebuilt in 1754.
Abdul Hamid I became Sultan of the Ottoman Empire and Caliph of Islam.
American Civil War: Jefferson Davis resigns from the United States Senate.
The first Monte Carlo Rally takes place.
Kiwanis International is founded in Detroit.
Albania declares itself a republic.
In Belmopan, Belize, the unrest over the government's new taxes erupts into riots.
The first contingent of 150 Swiss Guards arrives at the Vatican.
The Ava Kingdom falls to the Taungoo Dynasty in what is now Burma.
The Ashantis defeat British forces in the Gold Coast.
Columbia Phonograph is formed in Washington, D.C.
The United Mine Workers of America is founded in Columbus, Ohio.
Bloody Sunday in Saint Petersburg, beginning of the 1905 revolution.
Ramsay MacDonald becomes the first Labour Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
Israel withdraws from the Sinai Peninsula.
Apollo 5 lifts off carrying the first Lunar module into space.
Roman Emperor Theodosius I proclaims his eight-year-old son Honorius co-emperor.
The Royal Exchange opens in London.
The Union of Utrecht forms a Protestant republic in the Netherlands.
Blaise Pascal publishes the first of his Lettres provinciales.
The Principality of Liechtenstein is created within the Holy Roman Empire.
Second Partition of Poland.
Slavery in Tunisia is abolished.
Anglo-Zulu War: the Battle of Rorke's Drift ends.
The International Opium Convention is signed at The Hague.
World War II: German admiral Karl Dönitz launches Operation Hannibal.
The Knesset resolves that Jerusalem is the capital of Israel.
Diplomatic relations between the Soviet Union and Ivory Coast are established.
The Council of Basel suspends Pope Eugene IV.
Matthias Corvinus becomes king of Hungary.
King Charles II of England dissolves the Cavalier Parliament.
Charles VII Albert becomes Holy Roman Emperor.
California Gold Rush: James W. Marshall finds gold at Sutter's Mill near Sacramento.
Bucharest is proclaimed the capital of Romania.
The first Boy Scout troop is organized in England by Robert Baden-Powell.
Atocha massacre occurs in Madrid during the Spanish transition to democracy.
Apple Computer places the Macintosh personal computer on sale in the United States.
The United States Department of Homeland Security officially begins operation.
At least 35 die and 180 are injured in a bombing at Moscow's Domodedovo Airport.
Alfonso II becomes King of Naples.
Coronation of Francis I of France.
Henry VIII of England secretly marries his second wife Anne Boleyn.
Founding of São Paulo city, Brazil.
Moscow University is established on Tatiana Day.
The London Corresponding Society is founded.
The Bulgarian National Bank is founded.
Thomas Edison and Alexander Graham Bell form the Oriental Telephone Company.
Nellie Bly completes her round-the-world journey in 72 days.
Ukraine declares independence from Bolshevik Russia.
World War II: Thailand declares war on the United States and United Kingdom.
Florence Li Tim-Oi is ordained in China, becoming the first woman Anglican priest.
World War II: The Battle of the Bulge ends.
The United Mine Workers rejoins the American Federation of Labor.
The first Emmy Awards are presented; the venue is the Hollywood Athletic Club.
The Soviet Union ends the state of war with Germany.
Idi Amin leads a coup deposing Milton Obote and becomes Uganda's president.
Billy Bailey becomes the last person to be hanged in the U.S.A.
A stampede at the Mandhradevi temple in Maharashtra, India kills at least 258.
Vicente Yáñez Pinzón becomes the first European to set foot on Brazil.
The Lisbon earthquake kills about thirty thousand people.
Stanislaus I of Poland abdicates his throne.
Michigan is admitted as the 26th U.S. state.
Tennessee enacts the first prohibition law in the United States
Point No Point Treaty is signed in Washington Territory.
American Civil War: The state of Louisiana secedes from the Union.
Reconstruction Era: Virginia rejoins the Union.
Glenn H. Curtiss flies the first successful American seaplane.
The first demonstration of the television by John Logie Baird.
German-Polish Non-Aggression Pact is signed.
The Apollo Theater reopens in Harlem, New York City.
Soviet Union cedes Porkkala back to Finland.
Hindi becomes the official language of India.
Israel and Egypt establish diplomatic relations.
Song dynasty General Yue Fei is executed.
Dante Alighieri is exiled from Florence.
The Vatican opens the seven-year trial of scholar Giordano Bruno.
Boshin War: Tokugawa rebels establish the Ezo Republic in Hokkaidō.
Thomas Edison receives the patent on the incandescent lamp.
Ibn Saud takes the title of King of Nejd.
First flight of the Lockheed P-38 Lightning.
World War II: The 900-day Siege of Leningrad is lifted.
World War II: The Red Army liberates the remaining inmates of Auschwitz-Birkenau.
Nuclear testing at the Nevada Test Site begins with Operation Ranger.
The Soviet submarine S-80 sinks when its snorkel malfunctions, flooding the boat.
Germany first observes International Holocaust Remembrance Day.
The Diet of Worms begins, lasting until May 25.
Henry VIII dies. His nine-year-old son, Edward VI, becomes king.
Sir Horace Walpole coins the word serendipity in a letter to a friend.
Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice is first published in the United Kingdom.
Franco-Prussian War: The Siege of Paris ends in French defeat and an armistice.
Foundation of the Spanish Legion.
Japanese forces attack Shanghai.
Iceland becomes the first Western country to legalize therapeutic abortion.
Elvis Presley makes his first American television appearance.
The current design of the Flag of Canada is chosen by an act of Parliament.
The first boat specializing as a lifeboat is tested on the River Tyne.
Stamford Raffles lands on the island of Singapore.
Henry Clay introduces the Compromise of 1850 to the U.S. Congress.
Kansas is admitted as the 34th U.S. state.
Karl Benz patents the first successful gasoline-driven automobile.
The American League is organized in Philadelphia with eight founding teams.
Charles Curtis of Kansas becomes the first Native American U.S. Senator.
World War I: Paris is first bombed by German zeppelins.
The first inductees into the Baseball Hall of Fame are announced.
The first inductees into the Pro Football Hall of Fame are announced.
SCAT Airlines Flight 760 crashes near the Kazakh city of Almaty, killing 21 people.
The Second Temple of Jerusalem finishes construction.
Poland and the Holy Roman Empire conclude the Peace of Bautzen.
King Charles I of England is beheaded.
Yerba Buena, California is renamed San Francisco, California.
The first American ironclad warship, the USS Monitor is launched.
The first Anglo-Japanese Alliance is signed in London.
The Canadian Naval Service becomes the Royal Canadian Navy.
The Government of Turkey expels Patriarch Constantine VI from Istanbul.
The Politburo of the Soviet Union orders the extermination of the Kulaks.
Adolf Hitler is sworn in as Chancellor of Germany.
Mahatma Gandhi is assassinated by Nathuram Godse, a Hindu extremist.
Naro-1 becomes the first carrier rocket launched by South Korea.
Pope Sylvester I succeeds Pope Miltiades.
France cedes Naples to Aragon.
The Battle of Gembloux takes place.
The first venereal diseases clinic opens at London Lock Hospital.
John Marshall is appointed the Chief Justice of the United States.
John C. Frémont is court-martialed for mutiny and disobeying orders.
American Civil War: Confederate General Robert E. Lee becomes general-in-chief.
Czechoslav Trade Union Association is founded in Prague.
The Battle of George Square takes place in Glasgow, Scotland.
The Soviet Union exiles Leon Trotsky.
3M begins marketing Scotch Tape.
The first successful American satellite detects the Van Allen radiation belt.
Nauru gains independence from Australia.
The Chinese general Koxinga seizes the island of Taiwan after a nine-month siege.
The capital of Upper Canada is moved from Newark to York.
Slavery is abolished in Mauritius.
American Civil War: Texas secedes from the United States.
The first volume (A to Ant) of the Oxford English Dictionary is published.
Shinhan Bank, the oldest bank in South Korea, opens in Seoul.
Russia adopts the Gregorian calendar.
The United Kingdom recognizes the USSR.
Trygve Lie of Norway is picked to be the first United Nations Secretary-General.
A fire in the 25-story Joelma Building in São Paulo, Brazil kills 189 and injures 293.
The Communications Decency Act is passed by the U.S. Congress.
Conrad II, Holy Roman Emperor becomes king of Burgundy.
Nine leaders of the Transylvanian peasant revolt are executed at Torda.
Spaniard Pedro de Mendoza founds Buenos Aires, Argentina.
New Amsterdam (later renamed The City of New York) is incorporated.
Mexican-American War: The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo is signed.
Brigham Young declares war on Timpanogos in the Battle at Fort Utah.
In Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania the first Groundhog Day is observed.
Funeral of Queen Victoria.
Grand Central Terminal is opened in New York City.
France occupies Memel.
The Tartu Peace Treaty is signed between Estonia and Russia.
Ulysses by James Joyce is published.
The Export-Import Bank of the United States is incorporated.
Idi Amin replaces President Milton Obote as leader of Uganda.
Hama massacre: The government of Syria attacks the town of Hama.
After the 1986 People Power Revolution, the Philippines enacts a new constitution.
Soviet war in Afghanistan: The last Soviet armoured column leaves Kabul.
Sultan Mehmed II inherits the throne of the Ottoman Empire.
The colony of Massachusetts issues the first paper money in the Americas.
American Revolutionary War: Spain recognizes United States independence.
The Territory of Illinois is created by the 10th United States Congress.
Wake Forest University is established.
The Greco-Turkish War breaks out.
Space Shuttle program: STS-41-B is launched using Space Shuttle Challenger.
A Baghdad market bombing kills at least 135 people and injures a further 339.
Macapá, Brazil is founded.
The Riobamba earthquake strikes Ecuador, causing up to 40,000 casualties.
John Marshall is sworn in as Chief Justice of the United States.
The Royal Navy seizes Guadeloupe.
The Codex Sinaiticus is discovered in Egypt.
The Philippine-American War begins with the Battle of Manila.
Second Sino-Japanese War: Harbin, Manchuria, falls to Japan.
World War II: Santo Tomas Internment Camp is liberated from Japanese authority.
Ceylon (later renamed Sri Lanka) becomes independent within the British Commonwealth.
The Angolan War of Independence and the greater Portuguese Colonial War begin.
All Nippon Airways Flight 60 plunges into Tokyo Bay, killing 133.
In Guatemala and Honduras an earthquake kills more than 22,000.
A coup d'état is led by Hugo Chávez against Venezuelan President Carlos Andrés Pérez.
Earthquake in Pompeii, Italy.
South Carolina becomes the second state to ratify the Articles of Confederation.
Spanish defeat British forces and capture Menorca.
In Calabria, a sequence of strong earthquakes begins.
HMS Blenheim (1761) and HMS Java disappear off the coast of Rodrigues.
Peninsular War: Siege of Cádiz begins.
Jean-Baptiste Bernadotte ascends to the thrones of Sweden and Norway.
King Leopold II of Belgium establishes the Congo as a personal possession.
World War II: General Douglas MacArthur returns to Manila.
Gamal Abdel Nasser is nominated to be the first president of the United Arab Republic.
Astronauts land on the moon in the Apollo 14 mission.
Manuel Noriega is indicted on drug smuggling and money laundering charges.
A major tornado outbreak across the Southern United States kills 57.
Massachusetts becomes the sixth state to ratify the United States Constitution.
Battle of San Domingo: British naval victory against the French in the Caribbean.
New Jersey grants the first American railroad charter to John Stevens.
Sir Thomas Stamford Raffles founds Singapore.
Otto becomes the first modern King of Greece.
British women over the age of 30 get the right to vote.
The American Legion is founded.
World War II: The United Kingdom declares war on Thailand.
The Canadian Army enters combat in the Korean War.
Jack Kilby of Texas Instruments files the first patent for an integrated circuit.
Washington National Airport is renamed Ronald Reagan National Airport.
Father Mustaski is made a bishop.
Leo I the Thracian becomes emperor of the Byzantine Empire.
The 11th Amendment to the United States Constitution is ratified.
The strongest in a series of earthquakes strikes New Madrid, Missouri.
HMS Orpheus sinks off the coast of Auckland, New Zealand, killing 189.
Dreyfus affair: Émile Zola is brought to trial for libel for publishing J'accuse.
A fire in Baltimore, Maryland destroys over 1,500 buildings in 30 hours.
The second full-length animated Walt Disney film, Pinocchio, premieres.
The United States bans all Cuban imports and exports.
Grenada gains independence from the United Kingdom.
Pluto moves inside Neptune's orbit for the first time since either was discovered.
The Maastricht Treaty is signed, leading to the creation of the European Union.
NeXT merges with Apple Computer, starting the path to Mac OS X.
